correctness.rationale: PROOF vs EVIDENCE: The infinite claim G(n+148)=G(n) for all n>=259 is proved by finite computation plus a self-contained Guy-Smith propagation lemma (Lemma 1), not by extrapolation. Experimental corroboration (stability to 20000, p<=1000 scan) is clearly separated and not load-bearing. RULES VERIFIED: Octal 0.057 has d1=0,d2=5=101,d3=7=111,m=3. Auditor checked standard definition (bit0=take whole heap iff n==k, bit1=leave 1 heap, bit2=leave 2 heaps): d2=5 forbids singleton leave, d3=7 allows singleton+splits, d1=0 gives no moves. Boundary conditions recomputed by hand and code: G0=0, S1=empty=>G1=0, S2={0}=>G2=1, S3={0} (take-2 splits need a+b=1 impossible)=>G3=1, n=4 gives S4={0}=>G4=1. Table G0..40 matches recompute exactly. Sensitivity test: allowing take-2 singleton (digit 7) changes 43/51 values to N=50, so rule interpretation is material and correctly implemented. COMPUTATION VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: (1) Re-ran compute_grundy_0057.py to 8000: 0.73s, max 8, uniq {0,1,2,3,4,6,7,8}, byte-identical to logged CSV (diff -q IDENTICAL). (2) Independent pure-Python mex recompute to 2000: 0 mismatches. (3) Full stdlib mex recheck to 8000: 0 mismatches in 2.15s. (4) Extended recompute to 20000: 4.40s, zero mismatches on [259,19852], max still 8, zeros still {0,1}, reachset equality on final block still 148/148. (5) Ran verify_certificate_0057.py: CERTIFICATE PASS, all V1-V7 pass, 0.34s. LEMMA 1 LINE-BY-LINE VERIFIED: T*=2N0+2p+m=817. Hypothesis G(n)=G(n-p) on [N0+p=407,T] with T=8000>=817. Induction step N>T: singletons need N-3 in [N0+p,N-1] — holds since T-2>=N0+p because N0+p+m-2>=0. Splits A(S) with k=2,3, S=N-k>=2N0+2p+1, S'=S-p>=2N0+p+1: (subset) b=max(a,b)>=S/2>=N0+p+0.5 => b>=N0+p+1 integer and b<N, so G(b)=G(b-p) gives same xor in A(S'); (superset) d=max>=S'/2>=N0+1, j=d+p satisfies N0+p<j<N so G(j)=G(d) gives same xor in A(S). Terminal exclusion holds since N-p>=2N0+p+m+1>m=3. Threshold coverage 817<=7852 (=Nmax-p) verified. Suffix equality [259,7852] = 7594 agreements (~51 periods) verified 0 mismatches. REACHSET MECHANISM NOT OVERCLAIMED: V4 final-block S(n)=S(n+148) 148/148 verified; auditor additionally found full-range reachset equality fails at exactly 15 early indices [262,267,268,269,270,272,276,282,283,284,290,297,298,304,311] with max 311, and holds thereafter including final block — consistent with draft claiming equality only on final block. MINIMALITY CLOSES: V6a G258=2 vs G406=1 verified; V6b cycle C=G[259..406] has no cyclic subperiod (all p'<148 break; e.g. p=2:117 breaks, p=4:148, p=37:111, p=74:138) verified. Jointly sufficient: any period of infinite tail must be multiple of 148 (V6b), and any N0'<259 with such multiple fails at n=258 since G(258+k*148)=G406=1!=2 for all k>=1 by tail periodicity — draft's terse sketch is complete when V6a+V6b combined as §5 states. originality.rationale: SUBSTANTIVE COMPARISON (not timestamp): Nearest results are (a) Guy-Smith 1956 periodicity theorem + solved Kayles 0.77 / Dawson's Kayles 0.07 (period 34), (b) Flammenkamp octal survey tables to 1e5-1e6 scale, (c) Winning Ways Vol.1 / Siegel textbook octal chapter. (a) proves the general induction method invoked and solves different digits; take-2 digit 5 in 0.057 forbids the singleton leave that 0.07/0.77 allow, changing reachable sets A(N-2) — auditor sensitivity test confirms different sequence — so (259,148) is disjoint, not implied. (b) by nature supplies computed (conjectured, unproved) values without Guy-Smith window or mex-closure certificate; even if it lists 259/148 as observed, observation is not proof — the candidate's contribution is exactly the missing proof log (suffix equality + T*=817 + reachset equality). (c) is background (octal rules, mex) leaving 0.057-class as open tables/exercises. Period-scan uniqueness corroborates novelty of the pair: exhaustive p<=1000 longest-suffix scan gives only (259, multiples of 148) with N0<=400 and window>=3000; every other p first matches only at n>=6995 with window<=6 (end effects). Internal SCOPE prior scan checked: 8 validated findings (synchronizing automata, Heilbronn, Kronecker, forbidden families, RSBF, J2-free rank, 5x5 rank census, spider walks) and 18 failures (Henon, Z197 bases, Littlewood, matroids, Nash M22, balls-in-bins, Szemeredi-Trotter, sextuplets, Polya-Vinogradov, BH(6,3), codes, dicyclic, Latin, groups 96, curves F32, Ramsey-Turan, FEM, knots) — all disjoint objects/methods; nearest SCOPE-FAIL-20260907-013 (bimatrix Nash) explicitly distinguished as non-cooperative vs impartial heaps. No prior result states or proves ultimate Grundy periodicity (259,148) for 0.057 with induction certificate. A timestamp or failed search was not used as priority evidence.

value.rationale: INDEPENDENTLY WORTH FINDING LATER: Result is a durable exact classification of a canonical named game, not a textbook exercise. (1) Not textbook restatement: textbook gives the Guy-Smith lemma as a method; the new content is the exact minimal pair (259,148), 148-term cycle, and census (P={0,1}, max 8, tail values {1,2,4,7,8}) which no cited source proves. Lemma is re-proved self-contained with explicit loose threshold rather than cited. (2) Not parameter substitution: 0.057 is the splitting-dominant neighbour of solved Dawson's Kayles 0.07 (differs by restricting take-2 to no singleton leave), sits below 2.00, listed as computed-but-unproved survey entry; digit change alters move topology (verified material difference), not arbitrary S-vector. (3) Not tiny gain: first exact infinite proof (51-period base + induction to all n), not bound tweak; fallback 20000-table explicitly labelled as fallback, not claimed. (4) Not unexplained enumeration: mechanism explained and machine-checked (mex recomputation full-range 0 mismatches, reachset equality final block 148/148, threshold coverage). Consequence is citable: every heap n>=2 is N-position, all large-heap Grundy values known. Honest scope limits (§6) disclaim neighbours and general conjectures. Comparable octal periodicity closures (e.g. Dawson's Kayles period 34) are standard citable notes; this is of same kind for an unsolved entry.
